core.title: Exercise every declared timing semantic in a bound telemetry test
core.given: In an adopted repository, a tracking-plan item declares timing semantics (post-commit, absent-after-rollback, correlation-across-async) in its timing list
core.when: The item and its bound telemetry tests are evaluated — on any plan or test change, or for existing unchanged items (standing scope)
core.then: For each declared semantic, at least one test bound to the item must reference the corresponding behaviour (commit, rollback, correlation/context) in code or a test title.
prefer: Declare the timing semantic on the tracking-plan item, and name that behaviour in the bound test's title or assertions.
Assert the behaviour: emission only after commit, none after rollback, correlation context kept across the async handoff.
avoid: Satisfying a semantic only via a test comment or tracking-plan prose.
Relying on return-value tests for transaction-time telemetry.
Claiming the lexical check proves ordering statically — false precision.
unless: The item declares no timing (empty timing list, e.g. diagnostic logs, internal spans).
The rule family is not yet adopted: the rule is inert until adoption.
core.why: Transaction-time bugs (the event fired before its commit, the rollback that still emits, the context lost across an async handoff) escape return-value tests; the plan declares when ordering matters, so bound tests must speak to it.
evidence: For every adopted tracking-plan item with a non-empty timing list (changed or not), each declared semantic is matched by at least one test bound to the item whose code or test title references commit / rollback / correlation-context respectively.
The stack's telemetry-test check reports no timing-semantics finding.
verification: Semantic → behaviour mapping: post-commit = emission only after the transaction commits (probe for 'commit'); absent-after-rollback = never emitted when the transaction rolls back (probe for 'rollback'); correlation-across-async = correlation context continues across an async handoff (probe for 'correlation'/'context').

The check is plan-driven and lexical by design: the item's timing list is the source of truth, and a match counts only in test code or test titles — comments (comment syntax per the stack profile) and tracking-plan prose never satisfy. It deliberately does not prove ordering statically; it cannot, and pretending otherwise would be false precision.

Standing scope: every item with declared timing in an adopted repository is checked, each semantic independently, whether or not the item or its tests changed; only tests bound to the item (binding syntax from the profile) count, and only test files in the languages the profile declares for its telemetry tests are scanned. Items with an empty or absent timing list are not judged, which keeps diagnostic logs and internal spans out of scope. Inert until adoption, like every rule in this family.
Severity 3, disposition strict: the checker fails on every finding; there is no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

values: telemetry test (a test file bound to a tracking-plan item)
repository has adopted the telemetry rule family and its tracking plan contains any item with a non-empty timing list (standing state, whether the item, its bound tests, or neither changed)
declared timing semantic not referenced by any bound test

fires: A tracking-plan item declares post-commit and no test bound to it mentions commit in code or test title.
A plan-only change adds absent-after-rollback to an item whose existing, unchanged bound tests only assert return values, never rollback.
An existing, unchanged item declares correlation-across-async and the only mention of correlation/context is in a code comment or in the tracking-plan prose.
An item declares post-commit and absent-after-rollback, and bound tests reference commit but nothing references rollback.
doesNotFire: A diagnostic log or internal span whose tracking-plan item has an empty or absent timing list.
An item declaring only post-commit (its sole semantic) with a bound test whose title or assertions reference commit.
A repository that has not adopted the telemetry rule family (the rule is inert until adoption).

The language values (typescript, javascript) are the languages of the test files the check scans for behaviour references — a check-scope datum the profile carries as tooling.language_scopes#telemetry_tests (existing vocabulary v3 map entry), not the stack's production-source languages (which is why tooling.languages does not fit). The core folds this scope into its standing-scope verification ('only test files in the languages the profile declares for its telemetry tests are scanned'), so a stack realizing the core must declare its own telemetry-test languages there; the core itself adds no language condition, and its closed activation-fact vocabulary has no language fact, so no core activation fact is added. The note 'Bun realization.' is provenance only.

neutralityNotes: The tracking plan, the telemetry test and the three timing semantics (post-commit, absent-after-rollback, correlation-across-async), including the commit/rollback/correlation-context probes, are the rule family's own domain vocabulary and stay in the core; they are not stack-specific. Every stack-specific datum the core depends on comes through an existing vocabulary v3 key: the test-to-item binding construct (bun.json's 'Telemetry: header') via the parametric key urn.binding.telemetry, the tracking-plan plan-artifact kind via roles.plan_artifact.kinds, and the languages of the test files the check scans via the map entry tooling.language_scopes#telemetry_tests (bun.json's typescript/javascript activation fact — a check-scope datum over test files, not the stack's production-source languages, which is why tooling.languages does not fit). The core's standing-scope verification references that language scope, so a stack realizing the core must explicitly declare its telemetry-test languages there; the core adds no language condition of its own. The check's comment exclusion needs the stack's comment syntax (idiom.comment_marker), but bun.json never states it, so no bunValue could be given and it is only referenced from verification. Severity 3 and the strict disposition stay in core verification per the notProfileKeys rule, alongside the validator id bun_telemetry_test being Bun-only.
